source.title: Ax-Schanuel for Shimura varieties
source.authors: Ngaiming Mok, Jonathan Pila and Jacob Tsimerman
source.version: arXiv:1711.02189v3, posted 20 September 2018, 29 pages; v1 is from 6 November 2017. The arXiv abstract page carries no comment and no journal reference. The published text is behind the journal's paywall and was not consulted, so every locator gives the section, theorem, lemma or equation number together with the page of the arXiv v3 PDF, and any finding would be recorded against that version. No erratum or corrigendum is listed on the arXiv page or in Crossref.
readSections: §1 Introduction, pp. 1–4: Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4 and the discussion of weakly special subvarieties, Ax–Lindemann and Zilber–Pink
Part I, §2 Preliminaries, p. 5: definability, the definability of q on a Siegel fundamental set, Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 and Corollary 2.3
Part I, §3 Some algebraicity results, pp. 5–7: Theorem 3.1, Corollary 3.2, the Hilbert-scheme construction of §3.1 and Lemma 3.3
Part I, §4 Proof of Theorem 1.1, pp. 7–9: the triple induction, Lemmas 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3, with the Hwang–To and Pila–Wilkie inputs
Part II, §5 Jet spaces and §6 Differential equations, pp. 9–11: the definition of J^g_kX, the maps π_{a,b}, and the jet formulation of an algebraic differential equation

Part II, §7 Schwarzians for Hermitian symmetric domains, pp. 11–15: the setup, the Schwarzian equation W_m, nondegenerate jets, Lemma 7.1, Proposition 7.2, Corollary 7.3, Theorems 7.4 and 7.5 with Theorems A and B
Part II, §8 Connection formula and automorphic functions, pp. 15–16: the Schwarzian variety, ψ_k, the connection formula, Proposition 8.1 and Theorem 8.2
Part II, §§9–10, pp. 17–21: Theorem 9.1, Lemmas 9.2 and 9.4, Corollary 9.3, Lemmas 10.1–10.3 and Corollary 10.4
Part III, §11 Characterizing the uniformization map, pp. 22–24: Lemma 11.1, Theorems 11.2 and 11.3 and the foliation W_{n,ℓ}
Part III, §12 Ax-Schanuel in a differential field, pp. 24–26: the setting, rank and transcendence degree, uniformized loci and Theorem 12.3
Acknowledgements and References, pp. 26–29, read in full to identify the inputs listed under prerequisites

summary: Complete extraction of the 29-page paper proving the hyperbolic Ax–Schanuel conjecture. For a connected pure Shimura variety X = Γ\Ω with uniformization q : Ω → X and graph D ⊂ Ω × X, every irreducible component of W ∩ D of larger than expected dimension, for W ⊂ Ω × X algebraic, projects into a proper weakly special subvariety of X: all atypical intersections are accounted for by the bi-algebraic subvarieties. The proof combines o-minimality — the definability of q on a Siegel fundamental set, the definable Chow and Remmert–Stein theorems of Peterzil and Starchenko, and the Pila–Wilkie counting theorem — with the exponential volume growth of Hwang and To, the Zariski density of monodromy after André and Deligne, and a triple induction. The paper then proves a version with derivatives, for which it develops the Schwarzian differential equation of a Hermitian symmetric domain in jet spaces, showing that the G(ℂ)-translates of q are exactly the solutions of an algebraic differential system; this gives that a basis of modular functions with its partial derivatives to order at least 2 has transcendence degree dim G, generalising Bertrand–Zudilin. Finally it gives a differential-field version and shows that it implies the jet version. Of the 39 items, none is in the pinned libraries, 8 are planned by existing layers, and 31 are missing. The routing follows the atlas's own commitment: LD.6 plans o-minimality and Pila–Wilkie and names Ax–Schanuel among the inputs whose full proofs it must acquire, so the paper becomes a Part II of that roadmap, since Schwarzians, jet spaces, Ochiai's theorem and differential fields are new layers rather than additions to an o-minimality layer; the two definable GAGA theorems go to LD.6 itself, and weakly special subvarieties, which occur nowhere in the atlas, to ShimuraData D4 alongside the other distinguished classes. Five misprints were found and are recorded under sourceIssues; none affects a proof. This is a paper inventory and routing, not a proof blueprint: the results quoted from Peterzil–Starchenko, Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev, Hwang–To, André, Deligne, Ochiai, Mok, Pila–Wilkie, Seidenberg and Kazhdan are recorded as items with their own prerequisite entries and are not decomposed here.

items.name: The uniformization of a connected pure Shimura variety and algebraic subvarieties of Ω × X
items.statement: Let Ω be a Hermitian bounded symmetric domain attached to a semisimple group G and Γ ⊂ G(ℤ) a finite-index subgroup, so that X = Γ\Ω is a quasi-projective variety — a connected pure Shimura variety. Let q : Ω → X be the projection and D ⊂ Ω × X the graph of q. The domain Ω sits as an open subset of its compact dual Ω̂, a projective variety; an algebraic subvariety W ⊂ Ω × X means a complex-analytically irreducible component of Ŵ ∩ (Ω × X) for an algebraic Ŵ ⊂ Ω̂ × X.
items.note: The quasi-projectivity of Γ\Ω is Baily–Borel, planned at ShimuraVarieties V2 and V3; the Hermitian domain and its compact dual with the Borel embedding are planned at ShimuraData D2 and D3, and the arithmetic group with its properly discontinuous action at ShimuraVarieties V0 and V1. The bi-algebraic convention for subvarieties of Ω × X — algebraic in the compact dual, restricted to the domain — is the paper's own and is the shape in which every statement below is made.

items.name: Weakly special and special subvarieties
items.statement: A Shimura variety X carries a collection of weakly special subvarieties; the special subvarieties are those weakly special subvarieties containing a special point. Weakly special subvarieties are exactly the bi-algebraic subvarieties of X: their preimages in Ω are algebraic, so they give rise to atypical intersections — in the extreme case W = Ω₁ × X₁ with X₁ weakly special and Ω₁ a connected component of its preimage, one has dim W = dim U + dim X₁.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), §1, p. 2, referring to Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev for the description
items.note: The objects the main theorem is about, and the only source of atypical intersections it allows. Neither 'weakly special' nor 'bi-algebraic' occurs anywhere in the atlas; ShimuraData D4 plans the distinguished classes — special pairs, special points, Hodge and abelian type — and is the natural owner of the weakly special classes as well. Special subvarieties play no role in this paper.

items.name: Ax–Schanuel for Shimura varieties
items.statement: Let W ⊂ Ω × X be an algebraic subvariety and U an irreducible component of W ∩ D whose dimension is larger than expected, that is codim U < codim W + codim D, equivalently dim W < dim U + dim X. Then the projection of U to X is contained in a proper weakly special subvariety of X.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 1.1, p. 2; proved in §4, pp. 7–9
items.note: The hyperbolic Ax–Schanuel conjecture. For q = exp : ℂⁿ → (ℂ^×)ⁿ the statement is an equivalent form of Ax's theorem, although (ℂ^×)ⁿ is a mixed and not a pure Shimura variety and so is not formally covered. Every component of such an intersection has dimension at least dim W − dim X, so the theorem says that all atypical components are accounted for by weakly special subvarieties. It generalises the Ax–Lindemann theorem and is expected to play the role there that Ax–Lindemann plays for André–Oort, with applications to Zilber–Pink; Bakker–Tsimerman generalise it to variations of Hodge structure.

items.name: Transcendence degree of modular functions and their derivatives
items.statement: Let z₁, …, z_n be an N⁺(ℂ)-invariant algebraic coordinate system on Ω, where N⁺ ⊂ G is the unipotent radical of a parabolic opposite to the parabolic B defining Ω̂ = G/B, and let {φ₁, …, φ_N} be a ℂ-basis of modular functions. Then the field generated by the φ_i and their partial derivatives with respect to the z_j up to order k ≥ 2 has transcendence degree dim G over ℂ, and the same over ℂ(z₁, …, z_n).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 1.2, p. 3; proved as Corollary 9.3, p. 18
items.note: A generalisation of a result of Bertrand and Zudilin for Siegel modular varieties, with the caveat that their result holds over any algebraically closed subfield of ℂ whereas here there is no control over the field of definition of the differential equations.

items.name: Ax–Schanuel with derivatives, in coordinates
items.statement: Let V ⊂ Ω be an irreducible complex analytic variety not contained in a proper weakly special subvariety, let {z_i} be an algebraic coordinate system on Ω, and let {φ_j^{(ν)}} consist of a basis φ₁, …, φ_N of modular functions defined at at least one point of V together with their partial derivatives with respect to the z_j up to order k ≥ 2. Then tr.deg._ℂ ℂ({z_i}, {φ_j^{(ν)}}) ≥ dim G + dim V, all functions being restricted to V.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 1.3, pp. 3–4; proved as Corollary 10.4, p. 21
items.note: The jet-space-free consequence of Theorem 9.1, along the lines of the Pila–Tsimerman result for Cartesian powers of the j-function.

items.name: Differential Ax–Schanuel
items.statement: Let G, q and a differential field (K, D, C) with a finite set D of commuting derivations and constant field C be as in §12, and let (z, x, y) be a uniformized locus of rank k. Then tr.deg._C C(z, x, y) ≥ rank(z) + dim G, unless x is contained in a proper weakly special subvariety of X.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 1.4, p. 4, and Theorem 12.3, p. 25
items.note: The differential-field version, which in turn directly implies the jet version. It rests on the fact that all solutions of the relevant differential system are G-translates of q, which comes from the provenance of the system in the Schwarzian attached to G and Ω.

items.name: o-minimal structures, definable sets and the structure R_an,exp
items.statement: The language of o-minimal structures over a real closed field, definable sets and cell decomposition; throughout the paper 'definable' means definable in the o-minimal structure R_an,exp, whose o-minimality is due to van den Dries and Miller building on Wilkie.
items.note: LD.6 plans exactly this: 'Construct the selected o-minimal structures, definable sets and cell decomposition'. LD.0 plans the underlying first-order language and definability framework.

items.name: Definability of the uniformization on a Siegel fundamental set
items.statement: Let F be the classical Siegel domain for the action of Γ on Ω. Then the restriction q|_F of the uniformization to F is definable in R_an,exp. For a general Shimura variety this is due to Klingler, Ullmo and Yafaev, generalising results of Peterzil and Starchenko for moduli spaces of abelian varieties.
items.note: The bridge between the o-minimal and the Shimura-variety sides, without which none of §3 is available. LD.6 names 'definability of uniformization' among the inputs its applications are built from, but does not plan it for Shimura varieties, and neither ShimuraVarieties nor ShimuraData mentions definability; Siegel sets themselves are planned at ShimuraVarieties V0.

items.name: Definable Remmert–Stein
items.statement: Let M be a definable complex manifold and E a definable complex analytic subset of M. If A is a definable complex analytic subset of M − E, then its closure Ā is a complex analytic subset of M.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 2.1, p. 5, quoting Peterzil–Starchenko
items.note: One of the two definable GAGA-type theorems on which the paper's algebraicity results rest. LD.6 plans o-minimal structures, definable sets and cell decomposition and is the layer that should own this and the next two items, but its text does not mention them; a search of every stage description for 'Peterzil' and 'definable Chow' returns nothing.

items.name: Definable Chow
items.statement: Let Y be a quasiprojective algebraic variety and A ⊂ Y definable, complex analytic and closed in Y. Then A is algebraic. Consequently, if A ⊂ Y is definable and constructible complex analytic — that is, in the boolean algebra generated by closed complex analytic varieties — then A is constructible algebraic.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 2.2 and Corollary 2.3, p. 5
items.note: A slight strengthening of a theorem of Peterzil and Starchenko, obtained by combining their statement with definable Remmert–Stein; the same strengthening was observed by Scanlon and, in a less general form, by Pila and Tsimerman. The corollary follows by induction on dimension. This is the engine of §3: any Γ-invariant analytic set that is definable on a fundamental domain descends to an algebraic set.

items.name: Algebraicity of descended definable analytic sets
items.statement: Let A ⊂ Ω × X be a closed complex analytic set which is Γ × {id}-invariant and such that A ∩ (F × X) is definable. Then (q × id)(A) ⊂ X × X is a closed algebraic subset; if A is moreover constructible complex analytic, then (q × id)(A) is a constructible algebraic subset.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2, p. 6
items.note: The converse to the evident fact that the preimage of an algebraic subvariety is Γ-invariant, closed analytic and definable on a fundamental domain. It is proved in two lines from definable Chow, and it is the crucial new algebraicity observation of the paper.

items.name: Descending Hilbert-scheme loci
items.statement: Fix a smooth projective compactification X̂ of X, an algebraic W ⊂ Ω × X with Zariski closure Ŵ ⊂ Ω̂ × X̂, and U an irreducible component of W ∩ D. Let M be the Hilbert scheme of subvarieties of Ω̂ × X̂ with the Hilbert polynomial of Ŵ, B the universal family, A = {(z,x,y) : (z,x) ∈ W_y ∩ D} and, for each k, A(k) the closed analytic locus where the fibre dimension of θ : A → M at (z,x) is at least k. With ψ : Ω × X × M → Ω × X, put Z = Z(k) = ψ(A(k)). Then Z is closed, Γ-invariant and definable on F × X, so T = (q × id)(Z) ⊂ X × X is closed and algebraic.
items.note: The construction that turns the family of atypical intersections into an algebraic family on X × X, so that the monodromy theorem of André and Deligne can be applied to it. The paper notes that Lemma 3.3 can also be proved by the more geometric compactification methods of Mok and Mok–Zhong, using L² estimates for ∂̄.

items.name: The stabilizer of a very general member is finite
items.statement: In the setting of §3.1, let F₀ be the family of algebraic varieties corresponding to the irreducible component A(k)′ containing U × [W], let Γ₀ ⊂ Γ be the subgroup stabilizing every member of F₀, and let Θ be the identity component of the Zariski closure of Γ₀ in G(ℝ). Then Θ is a normal subgroup of G(ℝ) (Lemma 4.1), and Θ is the identity subgroup (Lemma 4.2).
items.note: Normality comes from the Zariski density of the monodromy group of V, via the properness of Γ\A(k)′ → V and stab(γ·W′) = γ stab(W′) γ^{-1}. Triviality is an induction: if Θ were positive-dimensional then G would be isogenous to Θ × Θ′, Ω and X would split accordingly, and the inductive hypothesis on the smaller factor would give dim U + dim X ≤ dim W, contradicting atypicality.

items.name: An atypical component forces an infinite stabilizer
items.statement: In the same setting, W is invariant by an infinite subgroup of Γ.
items.note: The counting argument. The definable set I = {γ ∈ G(ℝ) : dim_ℝ((γ·W) ∩ D ∩ (F × X)) = dim_ℝ U} contains every γ ∈ Γ for which U meets γF × X; the volume of (γ·W) ∩ D ∩ (F × X) is uniformly bounded, by the Siegel-coordinate covering of Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev, while by Hwang–To the volume of γ·W ∩ X ∩ B(R) grows exponentially in R, so I contains polynomially many integer matrices. Pila–Wilkie then produces real algebraic curves in I containing at least two integer points, and either W is stabilized by a nontrivial integer point or the induction on dim W − dim U or on dim U can be advanced.

items.name: The Pila–Wilkie counting theorem
items.statement: For a definable set in an o-minimal structure, the number of rational points of height at most T lying outside the algebraic part of the set is O_ε(T^ε); in particular a definable set containing more than polynomially many integer points of bounded height contains a positive-dimensional real algebraic subset.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in Lemma 4.3, p. 9, and Lemma 10.3, p. 21
items.note: LD.6 plans 'a source-complete Pila-Wilkie rational-point estimate outside the algebraic part with explicit height and epsilon quantifiers', and its acceptance condition insists that removing the algebraic part is essential.

items.name: Hwang–To volume growth for subvarieties of a Hermitian symmetric domain
items.statement: For an algebraic subvariety of a quotient of a Hermitian symmetric domain, the volume of its intersection with a hyperbolic ball of radius R grows exponentially in R.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in Lemma 4.3, p. 9, quoting Hwang and To
items.note: The complex-geometric input that, played against the uniform volume bound coming from definability, produces the polynomially many integer points required by Pila–Wilkie. It appears nowhere in the atlas: a search of every stage description for 'Hwang' returns nothing.

items.name: Zariski density of monodromy for subvarieties not contained in a weakly special subvariety
items.statement: A subvariety of a Shimura variety which is not contained in a proper weakly special subvariety has Zariski-dense monodromy group.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in §4, p. 7, and §10, p. 20, quoting André and Deligne
items.note: The group-theoretic input that makes Lemma 4.1 work. It is not planned: the atlas's monodromy layers are about local systems on curves and about the geometric monodromy of families, not about the Zariski closure of the monodromy of a subvariety of a Shimura variety.

items.name: Jet spaces and maps between them
items.statement: For X a smooth complex algebraic variety and k, g ≥ 1, set D^k_g = Spec ℂ[ε₁,…,ε_g]/M^{k+1} with M = (ε₁,…,ε_g), and define the jet space of order k by J^g_kX := Hom(D^k_g, X). Then J^g_0X = X, J^1_1X is the tangent bundle, J^g_k is a functor with natural projections J^g_k → J^g_r for k > r, and one writes J_kX for J^{dim X}_kX. The map φ : D^a_g × D^b_g → D^{a+b}_g induced by ε_i ↦ s_i + t_i gives natural maps π_{a,b} relating J_a J_b X and J_{a+b}X.
items.note: The setting in which Ax–Schanuel with derivatives is most naturally stated. Jet spaces of algebraic varieties are planned nowhere in the atlas: a search of every stage description for 'jet space' returns nothing.

items.name: Algebraic differential equations as jet subvarieties
items.statement: A holomorphic φ : ℂ^g → ℂ^g satisfying an algebraic differential equation of order m is recorded by the condition J_mφ ∘ id_m(ℂ^g) ⊂ W for a subvariety W ⊂ J_mℂ^g, where id_m : ℂ^g → J_mℂ^g is the natural section a ↦ (z ↦ a + ε). Replacing the target by any variety X, a differential equation is a subvariety W ⊂ J_mX, with no choice of local coordinates on the image. Differentiating the equation is the relation J_a id_b ∘ id_a = π_{a,b} ∘ id_{a+b}, which gives Im J_{a+b}φ ∘ id_{a+b} ⊂ π_{a,b}^{-1}(J_aW).
items.note: The coordinate-free formulation of an algebraic differential equation, worked out in the example φ′ = R(φ) where the relation φ″ = R(φ)R′(φ) is recovered geometrically. Not planned anywhere.

items.name: The Hodge decomposition of 𝔤 and the N⁺ coordinates on the compact dual
items.statement: Write Ω = G_ℝ/K with K maximal compact, so that Ω sits inside the flag manifold Ω̂ = G_ℂ/B for a complex parabolic B. The Lie algebra decomposes as 𝔤 = 𝔫⁻ ⊕ 𝔨_ℂ ⊕ 𝔫⁺, a Hodge structure of weight 2, with 𝔟 = 𝔫⁻ ⊕ 𝔨_ℂ and N^± the corresponding abelian unipotent groups. Fixing o ∈ Ω and an identification ℂⁿ ≅ N⁺ gives coordinates on an open subset of Ω̂ and compatible N⁺-invariant sections id_m : N⁺ → J_mN⁺.
items.note: The Hodge decomposition of the adjoint representation, the Borel embedding of Ω in the flag variety G/B and the parabolic stabilizing the Hodge filtration are planned at ShimuraData D2 and D3; the N⁺-coordinate charts and the compatible jet sections are the paper's own packaging of them.

items.name: The Schwarzian differential equation and nondegenerate jets
items.statement: Define the Schwarzian differential equation of order m to be W_m := G · id_m(N⁺) = G · id_m(o) ⊂ J_mΩ̂, the locus of jets of maps of the form z ↦ g·z. Define J^{nd,r}_kY ⊂ J^r_kY to be the locus of infinitesimal maps surjective on tangent spaces, which is nonempty only for r ≥ dim Y. For G = PSL₂, Ω = ℍ and m = 3 this recovers the classical Schwarzian derivative.
items.note: The differential equation satisfied by the uniformization map, and the reason all solutions of the relevant system are G-translates of q. The Schwarzian derivative of a Hermitian symmetric domain appears nowhere in the atlas.

items.name: Rigidity of the second-order infinitesimal neighbourhood
items.statement: The subgroup of B fixing id₁(o) is N⁻ (Lemma 7.1), and G acts freely on id₂(o), hence on all of J^{nd}_kΩ̂ for k ≥ 2 (Proposition 7.2). Consequently, if F : Ω̂ → Ω̂ satisfies J₃F ∘ id₃ ⊂ W₃, then F(z) = gz for some g ∈ G(ℂ) (Corollary 7.3).
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Lemma 7.1, Proposition 7.2 and Corollary 7.3, pp. 12–13
items.note: The freeness statement is what makes the Schwarzian a faithful invariant of a map up to G, and Corollary 7.3 is the characterisation of G-translates by third-order data that the connection formula converts into Theorem 8.2.

items.name: Lower-order rigidity in the ball and in rank at least two
items.statement: If n ≥ 2, Ω = B^n and G(ℂ) = PGL(n+1; ℂ), then a map f satisfying J₂f ∘ id₂ ⊂ W₂ is a G(ℂ)-translate (Theorem 7.4). If Ω is an irreducible bounded symmetric domain of rank at least 2 and G(ℂ) = Aut(Ω̂), then a map satisfying J₁f ∘ id₁ ⊂ W₁ is a G(ℂ)-translate (Theorem 7.5). Both extend to reducible Ω provided no irreducible factor is the disc, respectively provided every irreducible factor has rank at least 2.
items.note: Theorem 7.4 follows from a local holomorphic version of the Fundamental Theorem of Projective Geometry over ℂ (Theorem A, proved in Mok's book), and Theorem 7.5 from Ochiai's theorem characterising automorphisms of S-structures on an irreducible Hermitian symmetric space of compact type of rank at least 2 (Theorem B). They allow the order-3 hypothesis of Corollary 7.3 to be lowered in these cases.

items.name: The Schwarzian variety, the map ψ_k and the connection formula
items.statement: Define the k-th Schwarzian variety by S_k(Ω̂) := G\J_kΩ̂ ≅ B\J_kΩ̂(o) birationally, and for a rational F : Ω̂ → Ω̂ set S_k(F)(z) = G·J_kF(id_k(z)) ∈ S_k(Ω̂). There is a rational map ψ_k : S_k(Ω̂) × (N⁺\J_k(Ω̂)) → S_k(Ω̂), extended to powers, and for any two maps F₁, F₂ the connection formula ψ_k(S_k(F₁)(F₂(z)), J_kF₂(id_k(z))) = S_k(F₁ ∘ F₂)(z) holds.
items.note: For the upper half plane and k = 3 this is the classical Schwarzian and its classical composition law. The connection formula is the identity that lets the Schwarzian of the inverse uniformization be computed, and hence lets Proposition 8.1 be proved by descent.

items.name: Schwarzians of automorphic functions are algebraic
items.statement: Let Γ ⊂ G be discrete with X = Γ\Ω a Shimura variety, let φ = (φ₁, φ₂) : X → Ω̂² be a rational embedding and p_i = φ_i ∘ q. Then (S_k(p₁^{-1})(φ₁(x)), S_k(p₂^{-1})(φ₂(x))) is an algebraic function R_k(x) of x ∈ X.
items.note: Proved by observing that the expression is definable on a fundamental domain, by the connection formula and the definability of q|_F, and Γ-invariant, hence algebraic by definable Chow. A rational embedding into Ω̂² always exists because the function field of X is that of an irreducible hypersurface and Ω̂ is rational.

items.name: Characterisation of the uniformization by its Schwarzian
items.statement: Let U ⊂ Ω̂ be a connected open set and F : U → φ(X) ⊂ Ω̂² satisfy ψ₃(R₃(φ^{-1}(F(z))), J₃F(id₃(z))) = (S₃(id), S₃(id)). Then F(z) = p(gz) for some g ∈ G(ℂ).
items.note: The statement that the algebraic differential equation satisfied by the uniformization has, as its only solutions, the G(ℂ)-translates of it. By Theorems 7.4 and 7.5 one may use R₂ when Ω = B^n with n ≥ 2 and R₁ when Ω is irreducible of rank at least 2.

items.name: Ax–Schanuel with derivatives, in jet spaces
items.statement: Let k ≥ 2 and r ≥ dim X be positive integers and let W ⊂ J^{nd,r}_kΩ × J^{nd,r}_kX be an algebraic subvariety. Let U be an irreducible component of W ∩ J^{nd,r}_kD whose dimension is larger than expected, that is dim W < dim U + dim G. Then the projection of U to X is contained in a proper weakly special subvariety of X.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), Theorem 9.1, p. 17; proved in §10, pp. 20–21
items.note: The jet-space form of the main theorem, from which Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 follow as Corollaries 9.3 and 10.4. Note that the expected-dimension condition is now governed by dim G rather than dim X, because the graph of the jet prolongation of q has G(ℂ)-orbit of dimension dim G.

items.name: The jet graph has algebraic G-orbit and Zariski closure
items.statement: For k ≥ 2, the graph J^{nd,r}_kD ⊂ J^{nd,r}_kΩ × J^{nd,r}_kX of the jet prolongation J^r_kq is such that G(ℂ) · J^{nd,r}_kD is a closed algebraic subvariety and is the Zariski closure of J^{nd,r}_kD (Lemma 9.2); and for the analogue of the Hilbert-scheme locus Z in jet space, T = (q × id)(Z) ⊂ J^{nd,r}_kX × J^{nd,r}_kX is closed and algebraic (Lemma 9.4).
items.note: The two algebraicity inputs that let the argument of §§3–4 be rerun in jet space; both come from definable Chow through Theorem 8.2, which identifies the G-orbit as the solution set of an algebraic differential equation.

items.name: The jet-space analogue of the stabilizer argument
items.statement: With Θ defined as in §4 but for the jet-space family, Θ is a normal subgroup of G(ℝ) (Lemma 10.1), Θ is the identity subgroup (Lemma 10.2), and W is invariant by an infinite subgroup of Γ (Lemma 10.3); the contradiction proves Theorem 9.1.
items.note: The proofs follow §4, with the volume and counting arguments carried out on the jet spaces; Corollary 10.4 is then Theorem 1.3.

items.name: Finite-order jets determine a global group element
items.statement: For every positive integer k there is m = m(G, q, k) with the following property: if ∆_k is a k-dimensional disc and (w, u) : ∆_k → Ω̂ × Ω̂ is a pair of maps such that at every t there is g_t ∈ G(ℂ) with u(t) = g_t w(t) to order m, then there is a global g ∈ G(ℂ) with u(t) = g w(t).
items.note: The rigidity statement that turns a pointwise, infinitesimal condition into a global one, and hence makes the differential-algebraic characterisation of §11 possible.

items.name: Characterising the uniformization map by differential equations
items.statement: With m as above and V^k_m the corresponding jet locus, a map (w, u) : ∆_k → Ω̂ × X whose k-jet image lies in V^k_m satisfies u = q ∘ g ∘ w for a global g ∈ G(ℂ) (Theorem 11.2). Enlarging the data to (w, u, v) : ∆_k → Ω̂ × X × J^n_rX with image in V_{k,m} × V_{n,r}, tangent image in the integrable algebraic foliation W_{n,r}, and v restricting to u, one gets g ∈ G(ℂ) with (w, u, v) = L(w, g, r) (Theorem 11.3).
items.note: The foliation W_{n,r} is introduced precisely to force the group element to stay constant when w has a stabilizer; its leaves are the loci where g(t) ∈ gN, and the condition that v restrict to u then forces n(t) = id. The constructible algebraicity of V_{n,ℓ} and W_{n,ℓ} comes from Corollary 3.2.

items.name: Differential fields, rank and transcendence degree of a point
items.statement: Let (K, D, C) be a differential field with D = {D₁, …, D_d} a finite set of commuting derivations and C the constant field. For an algebraic variety V over C and p ∈ V(K), take an affine open U ∋ p over C, let S be the image of O(U) in K under evaluation at p, and define the transcendence degree of p to be tr.deg._C Frac(S) and the rank of p to be the rank of the matrix (D_i s)_{i,s}. For points p₁, p₂ of two varieties, p₂ is a function of p₁ if rank(p₁, p₂) = rank(p₂).
items.note: The differential-algebra vocabulary in which Theorem 1.4 is stated. A search of every stage description in the atlas for 'differential field' and 'differential algebra' returns nothing in this sense.

items.name: Uniformized loci of rank k in a differential field
items.statement: Fix a finite-type field of definition L₀ ⊂ ℂ for X and for the differential system satisfied by q, and a finite-type L ⊂ ℂ defining the constructible varieties of §11; assume C contains subfields Λ₀, Λ isomorphic to L₀, L under ι₀, ι. A K-point (z, x, y) of Ω̂ × X × J^n_rX with r ≥ 2, with x and z of the same rank k ≥ 1 and x a function of z, satisfying the differential conditions of Theorem 11.3, is a uniformized locus of rank k; under a Seidenberg embedding over ι it becomes an honest tuple of regular functions on a k-dimensional disc.
items.note: The weakly special families come in countably many families defined over ℚ̄ and stable under Galois, so they may be taken to be defined over L₀, which is what makes 'x is contained in a weakly special subvariety' a condition on a K-point.

items.name: Seidenberg's embedding theorem
items.statement: Any finitely generated differential field extension of ℚ embeds into a field of meromorphic functions on some domain, compatibly with a given embedding of the constants.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in §12.3, pp. 24–25, in the version given by Scanlon
items.note: The device that converts a differential-algebraic statement into a statement about actual holomorphic functions on a disc, where Theorem 9.1 applies. It appears nowhere in the atlas.

items.name: Conjugates of arithmetic varieties are arithmetic
items.statement: A conjugate of an arithmetic variety is again arithmetic.
items.locator: arXiv:1711.02189v3 (20 September 2018), used in §12.1, p. 24, quoting Kazhdan, see also Milne
items.note: Quoted as a deep theorem, and needed to ensure that the differential fields considered are identified correctly with the complex objects. It is not planned; ShimuraVarieties V7 plans Milne's conjugation and descent theory for Shimura varieties, which is adjacent but is a statement about canonical models rather than about arithmeticity of conjugates.

items.name: Complex analytic sets, Chow's theorem and Remmert–Stein
items.statement: Closed complex analytic subsets of a complex manifold, their local dimension theory and irreducible components, Chow's theorem that a closed analytic subset of projective space is algebraic, and the Remmert–Stein extension theorem across an analytic subset of smaller dimension.
items.note: ComplexComparisonPartII C4 plans Chow algebraization and morphism comparison, and C0–C3 the analytic coherent theory it rests on. The definable versions used here are separate items.

items.name: Hilbert schemes of a projective variety
items.statement: The Hilbert scheme parametrising closed subschemes of a projective variety with a fixed Hilbert polynomial, with its universal family and its projectivity.
items.note: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.2 plans the Hilbert and Quot functors and R09.1 the projective parameter spaces. The compactness of M is what makes ψ proper and Z closed.

items.name: Arithmetic groups, Siegel sets and fundamental domains
items.statement: Arithmetic subgroups of a semisimple group acting on a Hermitian symmetric domain, reduction theory, Siegel sets and the existence of a fundamental set with finitely many translates covering the quotient.
items.note: ShimuraVarieties V0 plans arithmeticity and commensurability, the reduction theory consumed from AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups and ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces including rational parabolics and Siegel sets, and the existence of neat congruence subgroups with properly discontinuous action.

items.name: The Baily–Borel algebraic structure on an arithmetic quotient
items.statement: An arithmetic quotient Γ\Ω of a Hermitian symmetric domain is a quasi-projective algebraic variety, with a minimal compactification.
items.note: ShimuraVarieties V2 plans Baily–Borel algebraicity and the minimal compactification and V3 Borel algebraicity and uniqueness; V1 plans the analytic tower.

prerequisites.citation: Ya'acov Peterzil and Sergei Starchenko, Tame complex analysis and o-minimality, Proc. ICM 2010, and Complex analytic geometry in a nonstandard setting, in Model Theory with Applications to Algebra and Analysis, LMS Lecture Note Ser. 349
prerequisites.why: The definable Remmert–Stein theorem (65.3) and the definable Chow theorem (4.5) on which every algebraicity statement in §3 rests, and the definability of the uniformization for moduli of abelian varieties that Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev generalise.

prerequisites.citation: Bruno Klingler, Emmanuel Ullmo and Andrei Yafaev, The hyperbolic Ax–Lindemann–Weierstrass conjecture, Publ. Math. IHÉS 123 (2016), 333–360
prerequisites.why: The definability of q on a Siegel fundamental set for a general Shimura variety, and the Siegel-coordinate covering of Lemma 5.8 that gives the uniform volume bound used in Lemma 4.3. It is also the Ax–Lindemann theorem that Theorem 1.1 generalises.

prerequisites.citation: Jonathan Pila and Alex J. Wilkie, The rational points of a definable set, Duke Math. J. 133 (2006), 591–616
prerequisites.why: The counting theorem used in Lemmas 4.3 and 10.3 to produce real algebraic curves through many integer points. LD.6 plans it, so it is listed here only because the atlas has not yet acquired the proof.

prerequisites.citation: Jun-Muk Hwang and Wing-Keung To, Volumes of complex analytic subvarieties of Hermitian symmetric spaces, Amer. J. Math. 124 (2002), 1221–1246
prerequisites.why: Theorem 2 there gives the exponential growth in R of the volume of an algebraic subvariety intersected with a hyperbolic ball of radius R, which is what forces the definable set I to contain polynomially many integer points.

prerequisites.citation: Yves André, Mumford–Tate groups of mixed Hodge structures and the theorem of the fixed part, Compositio Math. 82 (1992), 1–24, and Pierre Deligne, Un théorème de finitude pour la monodromie, in Discrete Groups in Geometry and Analysis, Progr. Math. 67
prerequisites.why: The theorem that a subvariety of a Shimura variety not contained in a proper weakly special subvariety has Zariski-dense monodromy, quoted as André–Deligne and used to prove that Θ is normal in G(ℝ).

prerequisites.citation: Takushiro Ochiai, Geometry associated with semisimple flat homogeneous spaces, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 152 (1970), 159–193
prerequisites.why: Ochiai's theorem characterising automorphisms of S-structures on an irreducible Hermitian symmetric space of compact type of rank at least 2, which is Theorem B and gives Theorem 7.5.

prerequisites.citation: Ngaiming Mok, Metric Rigidity Theorems on Hermitian Locally Symmetric Manifolds, Series in Pure Mathematics 6, World Scientific, 1989
prerequisites.why: Section (2.3) contains the local holomorphic version of the Fundamental Theorem of Projective Geometry over ℂ, Theorem A, which gives Theorem 7.4; the same book's compactification and L²-estimate methods are the alternative route to Lemma 3.3 the paper mentions.

prerequisites.citation: James Ax, On Schanuel's conjectures, Ann. of Math. 93 (1971), 252–268
prerequisites.why: The original Ax–Schanuel theorem, which Theorem 1.1 specialises to for q = exp, and which is given a new proof by Pila–Tsimerman in the paper's reference [38].

prerequisites.citation: Jonathan Pila and Jacob Tsimerman, Ax–Schanuel for the j-function, Duke Math. J. 165 (2016), 2587–2605
prerequisites.why: The case of Cartesian powers of the j-function, including the version with derivatives that Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 generalise, and the model for the proof strategy of §4.

prerequisites.citation: Thomas Scanlon, Algebraic differential equations from covering maps, Adv. Math. 330 (2018), 1071–1100
prerequisites.why: The general result that covering maps satisfy algebraic differential equations, the strengthening of definable Chow observed there as Theorem 2.11, and the version of the Seidenberg embedding theorem used in §12.

prerequisites.citation: Daniel Bertrand and Wadim Zudilin, On the transcendence degree of the differential field generated by Siegel modular forms, J. reine angew. Math. 554 (2003), 47–68
prerequisites.why: The transcendence-degree result for Siegel modular varieties that Theorem 1.2 generalises, over any algebraically closed subfield of ℂ — a strengthening this paper does not obtain.

prerequisites.citation: David Kazhdan, On arithmetic varieties, in Lie Groups and their Representations (1975), and Arithmetic varieties and their fields of quasi-definition, Actes ICM 1970; see also J. S. Milne, The action of an automorphism of ℂ on a Shimura variety and its special points
prerequisites.why: The theorem that a conjugate of an arithmetic variety is arithmetic, quoted as deep and needed in §12.1 to identify the differential fields correctly with the complex objects.

prerequisites.citation: Christopher Daw and Jinbo Ren, Applications of the hyperbolic Ax–Schanuel conjecture, Compositio Math. 154 (2018), 1843–1888; Benjamin Bakker and Jacob Tsimerman, The Ax–Schanuel conjecture for variations of Hodge structures, Invent. Math. 217 (2019), 77–94
prerequisites.why: The first application of Theorem 1.1 to the Zilber–Pink conjecture, and the generalisation to variations of Hodge structure. They are the downstream consumers that make the routing to the unlikely-intersections layer the right one.

routes.title: Logic, definability, valued fields and motivic integration, Part II: functional transcendence and Ax–Schanuel for Shimura varieties
routes.brief: Extend the roadmap Logic, definability, valued fields and motivic integration in the direction its o-minimality layer LD.6 already points: functional transcendence for the uniformization of a Shimura variety, following Mok, Pila and Tsimerman, Annals of Mathematics 189 (2019). LD.6 plans o-minimal structures, cell decomposition, the Pila–Wilkie counting theorem and Pila–Zannier applications, and names 'independent Galois-orbit and Ax-Lindemann/Ax-Schanuel inputs' among the primary proofs it must acquire; this Part II supplies those inputs, which need layers of their own because their proofs are not model theory but complex geometry, the group theory of Hermitian symmetric domains, and differential algebra. The final theorems are these. (1) Ax–Schanuel for Shimura varieties (Theorem 1.1): for X = Γ\Ω a connected pure Shimura variety with uniformization q : Ω → X and graph D ⊂ Ω × X, if W ⊂ Ω × X is algebraic and U is an irreducible component of W ∩ D with dim W < dim U + dim X, then the projection of U to X lies in a proper weakly special subvariety. (2) Ax–Schanuel with derivatives (Theorem 9.1): the same statement in the jet spaces J^{nd,r}_kΩ × J^{nd,r}_kX with the expected-dimension condition governed by dim G, and its two corollaries — that a basis of modular functions together with its partial derivatives to order k ≥ 2 has transcendence degree dim G over ℂ and over ℂ(z), and that restricted to a variety V not inside a proper weakly special subvariety the transcendence degree is at least dim G + dim V. (3) Differential Ax–Schanuel (Theorem 12.3): for a differential field (K, D, C) and a uniformized locus (z, x, y) of rank k, tr.deg._C C(z, x, y) ≥ rank(z) + dim G unless x lies in a proper weakly special subvariety. Cover, in layers: weakly special subvarieties and their bi-algebraicity, imported from the source route proposed alongside this one; the definability of q on a Siegel fundamental set, after Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev and Peterzil–Starchenko, and the algebraicity principle it yields — a Γ-invariant closed analytic set definable on a fundamental domain descends to an algebraic subset of X × X; the Hilbert-scheme family of atypical intersections and its descent; the stabilizer argument, with the Zariski density of monodromy after André and Deligne, the exponential volume growth of Hwang–To, the uniform volume bound coming from definability, and the Pila–Wilkie counting theorem, assembled into the triple induction on dim Ω, on dim W − dim U and on dim U; jet spaces of algebraic varieties with the maps π_{a,b}, and algebraic differential equations as jet subvarieties together with the geometric form of differentiating an equation; the Hodge decomposition 𝔤 = 𝔫⁻ ⊕ 𝔨_ℂ ⊕ 𝔫⁺, the N⁺-coordinates on the compact dual, and the Schwarzian differential equation W_m = G · id_m(o) with the nondegenerate jet loci; the rigidity results — B fixes id₁(o) exactly on N⁻, G acts freely on id₂(o), a map with J₃ in W₃ is a G(ℂ)-translate, and the lower-order versions in the ball via the Fundamental Theorem of Projective Geometry and in rank at least 2 via Ochiai's theorem; the Schwarzian variety, the map ψ_k, the connection formula, the algebraicity of the Schwarzian of an automorphic function, and the resulting characterisation of q up to G(ℂ); the jet-space forms of all of the above; and finally the differential-field package — rank and transcendence degree of a K-point, the foliation that keeps the group element constant, uniformized loci, and the Seidenberg embedding that turns a differential-algebraic hypothesis into holomorphic functions on a disc. Every definition gets its API and unit tests, and the two quoted external theorems that are not proved here, Hwang–To volume growth and Kazhdan's theorem that a conjugate of an arithmetic variety is arithmetic, are recorded with their hypotheses. Import, never re-plan: o-minimal structures, definable sets, cell decomposition and the Pila–Wilkie theorem from LD.6 and LD.0, together with the definable Remmert–Stein and definable Chow theorems that this extraction routes to LD.6; Hermitian symmetric domains, the compact dual, the Borel embedding and the Hodge decomposition of the adjoint representation from ShimuraData D2 and D3, and the weakly special classes from D4; arithmetic groups, Siegel sets and fundamental sets from ShimuraVarieties V0 and ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0; the analytic tower and Baily–Borel algebraicity from ShimuraVarieties V1, V2 and V3; Chow's theorem and the analytic comparison from ComplexComparisonPartII C2 and C4; and Hilbert schemes from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1 and R09.2. Record as downstream, not as targets here, the applications to Zilber–Pink and André–Oort that LD.6 owns.
routes.reason: LD.6 is the layer this paper serves, and it says so itself: its construct-and-export text builds Pila–Zannier applications 'from separate Galois-orbit bounds, definability of uniformization and functional-transcendence theorems', and its source route lists 'independent Galois-orbit and Ax-Lindemann/Ax-Schanuel inputs. Record the exact full proof for each.' So the atlas already commits to acquiring this proof, and the question is only where it goes. It cannot go inside LD.6: that layer is about o-minimal structures, definable sets, cell decomposition and rational-point counting, whereas the bulk of this paper is complex geometry and group theory — the Schwarzian differential equation of a Hermitian symmetric domain, jet spaces, Ochiai's theorem, Hwang–To volume growth, the André–Deligne monodromy theorem — and differential algebra. Those are new layers in LD.6's direction, which is what PROTOCOL.md section 15 calls a Part II. A new roadmap was rejected because the whole point of the theorem is to feed the unlikely-intersection programme LD.6 owns, and because the o-minimal half of the proof is exactly LD.6's subject; a source route was rejected because none of the layers of the parent roadmap plans jets, Schwarzians or differential fields. The parent is a campaign roadmap, not a Tau Ceti one, so either route was formally available.

Definable Remmert–Stein and definable Chow, in the form used here, are theorems of o-minimality with no Shimura content: a definable complex analytic subset of a quasiprojective variety, closed in it, is algebraic, and the constructible version follows by induction on dimension. LD.6 plans 'the selected o-minimal structures, definable sets and cell decomposition' and is the layer that should own them, but its text does not mention them and a search of every stage description in the atlas for 'Peterzil' and 'definable Chow' returns nothing. They are routed here rather than into the Part II proposed alongside because every consumer of o-minimality in the atlas will want them, not only the functional-transcendence layers: they are the definable form of GAGA. This is a source route on an existing layer of the same roadmap whose Part II takes the rest of the paper, and the two are complementary — the source adds to a layer that exists, the Part II adds layers that do not.

D4 constructs the category of Shimura data with its products, adjoint passage and central isogenies, and defines the distinguished classes: special pairs, special points, Hodge type, abelian type and pre-abelian type. Weakly special subvarieties belong to exactly that list — they are the bi-algebraic subvarieties, the images of sub-data crossed with a point, and the special subvarieties are precisely the weakly special ones containing a special point, a definition that D4 already has half of. A search of every stage description in the atlas for 'weakly special' and 'bi-algebraic' returns nothing, so the notion is missing, and PROTOCOL.md section 15 asks that a general missing notion be planned once in the layer that owns its neighbours. The Part II proposed alongside then imports it rather than defining it, which matters because every statement in this paper has 'is contained in a proper weakly special subvariety' as its conclusion.
